Kuvitus: ulkoilmakonsertti iltahämärissä: Illustration: an open-air concert at dusk. On both sides of the stage are tall speaker towers, from which arcs of sound waves go towards the audience. On the stage a performer raises both hands under the spotlights. In the foreground is an audience seen from behind, and in the middle one listener wears red ear defenders.
Kaavakuva: pystysuora desibeliasteikko 2: Schematic figure: a vertical decibel scale from 20 decibels to 130 decibels, drawn to scale. To the right of the scale are typical sound levels: a whisper about 30 dB, a conversation about 60 dB, a lawn mower about 90 dB, a rock concert about 105 dB and the threshold of pain about 120 dB. The upper part of the scale from 85 decibels upwards is coloured red and marked on the left with a bracket: long exposure to such a high level damages hearing.
Pylväskuvaaja mittakaavassa: sallittu pä: Bar chart to scale: the permitted daily exposure time t in hours as a function of the noise level L. At a noise level of 85 dB the time is 8 hours, at 88 dB 4 hours, at 91 dB 2 hours, at 94 dB 1 hour, at 97 dB 0.5 hours and at 100 dB 0.25 hours. Every rise of three decibels halves the height of the bar.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: melun torju: Schematic figure, not to scale: the three points of noise control from left to right. On the left a machine is inside a casing: the source. In the middle is a noise wall, over which sound waves bend, weakened: the path. On the right a person's head has hearing protectors: the ear. Under each point is a measure: enclosure, barrier and distance, hearing protector.
Kaavakuva huoneesta sivulta, ei mittakaa: Schematic figure of a room from the side, not to scale. On the left a loudspeaker, on the right a listener's head at the same height. The direct sound travels horizontally from the loudspeaker to the listener. The reflected sounds, drawn with dashed lines, travel via the ceiling and the floor: they are reflected from the surfaces according to the law of reflection and reach the listener after a longer distance, that is, later than the direct sound.
Kuvaaja: äänitaso L desibeleinä ajan t f: Graph: sound level L in decibels as a function of time t, when the sound source falls silent at time zero. In both rooms the level is at first 90 dB and falls steadily. In the classroom with bare surfaces (blue) the level has fallen by 60 dB, to 30 dB, in 1.2 seconds, and in the classroom damped with acoustic panels (green) already in 0.6 seconds. These times are the reverberation times.
Kaavakuva: kolme aaltoa allekkain samall: Schematic figure: three waves one below the other on the same time axis. At the top the blue noise, in the middle the orange anti-noise, which is similar but in the opposite phase: its peak is at the trough of the noise. At the bottom their sum, which is a straight line at zero. A vertical dashed line shows that the peak and the trough coincide at the same moment.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa, kaksi osaa: Schematic figure, not to scale, in two parts side by side. On the left a loudspeaker from the side: a permanent magnet with a coil around its central pole, and a cone attached to the coil. The wires to the coil bring the alternating current, and a double-headed arrow in front of the cone shows that the cone vibrates. Below, the energy conversion: signal, motion, sound. On the right a microphone: sound waves arrive from the right at a diaphragm that is attached to a coil around the pole of a magnet, and a voltage is obtained from the wires of the coil. Below: sound, motion, signal.
